SUPERVISOR: new task — REQBOARD-0607. The request ledger evolves from two states into a four-state job board. User ruling, verbatim anchors: "so there are 4 states 1 new 2 in process 3 review 4 done" and "no longer takes every single message of mine and makes a request, since a number of them are me just sending perf logs for bug hunting". Jobs now enter ONLY via an explicit marker or via the supervisor; only the user (relayed through the supervisor) flips review→done. Do all of this yourself in your own context — no subagents.

Files: docs/game/_index/requests.ts, requestCli.ts, requests.test.ts, docs/game/REQUESTS.md, the ledger rule section in CLAUDE.md, and the oracle's REQUEST LEDGER tier in oracle.ts if it filters by status. The by-addition laws stay absolute: ask text BYTE-VERBATIM forever, entries never deleted, history never rewritten.

Step 1 — data model (requests.ts):
- RequestStatus becomes 'new' | 'doing' | 'review' | 'done'. parseEntry NORMALIZES legacy values on read: 'open'→'new', 'resolved'→'done' (old files stay readable forever).
- Each record gains an append-only `events` array: {at: ISO, actor: string, kind: 'state'|'note', from?, to?, text?}. Notes and transitions only ever append.
- Legal transitions, enforced in one function: new→doing (worker claims), doing→review (REQUIRES resolution paragraph ≥ MIN_RESOLUTION_CHARS + shas — the existing resolve discipline relocates here), review→done (gated: only actor 'user' — the supervisor relays the user's word), review→new (bounce, note required), new→done (supervisor-only noise-close for triage, note required; NEVER from doing/review). done is terminal. Everything else rejected with a message naming the legal moves.
- Resolution fields (resolution/shas/resolvedAt) are filled at the doing→review move, exactly once, never rewritten — done is acceptance only.

Step 2 — CLI (requestCli.ts):
- `board [--since <ISO>]`: the four columns with counts and compact rows (id, age, origin, first 80 chars of ask). With --since, append an ACTIVITY section: every event after that timestamp (id, transition/note, actor). This is the supervisor's loop tool.
- `move <id> <state> --by <actor> [--para "..."] [--shas sha,sha|none] [--note "..."]` — validates via the step-1 transition function.
- `note <id> --by <actor> "text"`.
- `log` unchanged (manual post, lands in new).
- `resolve <id> --para --shas` is REDEFINED as an alias for `move <id> review` — workers' existing habit now lands work in review, not done. Say so in the CLI help loudly.
- `migrate-board` — one-shot: rewrite every entry's legacy status to the mapped value (open→new, resolved→done), idempotent, prints counts. Nothing else about an entry is touched.

Step 3 — hook capture (hookCapturePrompt):
- Blanket capture DIES. Config gains `jobMarkers: string[]` (default ['JOB:']). A prompt is captured iff it starts with a marker (store verbatim INCLUDING the marker) → state new. dispatchPrefixes behavior is unchanged (SUPERVISOR dispatches still captured as origin supervisor-dispatch, still exempt). Every other prompt: skipped — perf logs, steering, banter never become requests again.
- Stop-hook reminder now scans only entries the session has in 'doing'.

Step 4 — tests (requests.test.ts): legacy normalization on read; every legal transition; every illegal transition rejected (especially worker attempting review→done and any move out of done); para+shas demanded at doing→review; marker-only capture (marker hit, marker miss, dispatch prefix); migrate-board idempotence; events append-only ordering.

Step 5 — docs: REQUESTS.md rewritten for the board (states, transitions, who may move what, the marker). CLAUDE.md ledger rule updated: worker contract is claim (move doing) → work → move review with paragraph + SHAs → STOP; done is never yours to flip. Oracle tier updated if it special-cases 'open'.

Step 6 — run `tools/request migrate-board` once, then `./tools/rjit game verify` green, then post READY with: file list, test count, board output sample, migration counts. NO commit — commit comes on my word after verification.
